note: Corps of Engineers campground on Cheatham Lake, the impounded Cumberland River just upstream of Cheatham Lock and Dam, with a boat ramp, swimming area and playground. The riverside row (sites 27-35) backs onto an open mown bank at the water; a few sites are under 23 ft. --Claude
summary: Operating USACE campground, 44 sites (37 standard electric to 40 ft + 7 tent electric), all 50A + water, showers/flush toilets/dump, reservation-only on rec.gov Apr 1-Oct 30, 2-night weekend minimum. Rates rise April 2027 to $28 standard / $32 riverside (2026 $24/$28). Imagery and rec.gov site photos show the riverside row is waterfront, not riverview.
flags: WATERFRONT UPGRADE CANDIDATE: stored 'riverview' -> propose 'riverfront' (the Cheatham pool here is ~200 m wide river). Named sites 27 (36 ft), 28 (38 ft), 29 (40 ft), 30 (40 ft), 31 (40 ft), 33 (40 ft) - catalog coordinates 36.31536,-87.18819 / 36.31540,-87.18849 / 36.31542,-87.18890 / 36.31546,-87.18917 / 36.31549,-87.18932 / 36.31552,-87.18963 - sit ~15-25 m from the water's edge over an open mown apron with only scattered single trees (Esri z19), and the rec.gov preview photos for 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 33 show the pad running to a picnic table with the river directly behind, no tree line, bank low and grassy (passes the kayak test). All are standard electric sites sold nightly on rec.gov ($28 riverside template now, $32 from April 2027). Cheatham is a run-of-river pool with little drawdown, so the pictured edge is the summer edge. Sites 37 (22 ft) and 38 (18 ft) are also on the water but too short. The stored evidence ('thin/scattered bank treeline, continuous tree screen') does not match the imagery or the site photos.
